## Overview

This vignette shows the local IV-GMM workflow built on `gmm_dnn()`. The example
uses the doubly robust IV moment model created by `gmm_model_dr_iv()` and the IV
simulation DGPs exposed through `sim_iv_data()`.

The full paper replication grid is intentionally kept out of the vignette. It is
installed with the package under `inst/paper-replication/iv/` and can be located
after installation with:

```{r replication-path, eval = FALSE}
system.file("paper-replication/iv/run.R", package = "RdistNN")
system.file("paper-replication/iv/hpc", package = "RdistNN")
```

## One Local IV Dataset

`sim_iv_data()` returns a data frame with observed variables, oracle nuisance
columns, the target point `x0`, and the true local IV target `theta_x0`.

```{r dgp}
iv <- sim_iv_data(
  design = "dgp2_iv_homog_overid",
  n = 160L,
  kx = 2L,
  q = 2L,
  seed = 1L
)

head(iv$data[, c("X1", "X2", "Z1", "Z2", "D", "Y")])
iv$theta_x0
```

## Fitting the DR-IV GMM Model

The DR-IV model factory records which columns contain the outcome, treatment,
instruments, and nuisance estimates. In this example the nuisance columns are
oracle values generated by the DGP.

```{r fit}
model_iv <- gmm_model_dr_iv(
  y_col = "Y",
  d_col = "D",
  z_cols = c("Z1", "Z2"),
  pi_cols = c("piZ1_oracle", "piZ2_oracle"),
  muY_col = "muY_oracle",
  muD_col = "muD_oracle"
)

fit_iv <- gmm_dnn(
  data = iv$data,
  x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  x0 = iv$x0,
  model = model_iv,
  k = 2L,
  s = 12L,
  se = TRUE,
  return = "ess"
)

fit_iv$theta
fit_iv$se
fit_iv$J
fit_iv$pval_J
fit_iv$neff
```

`summary()` and `confint()` expose the same fitted object in reporting form:

```{r methods}
summary(fit_iv)
confint(fit_iv)
```

## Small IV Simulation

`sim_iv_run()` expands a grid over designs, sample sizes, covariate dimensions,
instrument counts, and Monte Carlo replications. The just-identified design
`dgp1_iv_justid_linear` is always run only once with realized `q = 1`.

```{r small-run}
raw_iv <- sim_iv_run(
  designs = c("dgp1_iv_justid_linear", "dgp2_iv_homog_overid"),
  n_vals = 120L,
  kx_vals = 2L,
  q_vals = 2L,
  n_reps = 2L,
  master_seed = 42L,
  k = 1L,
  s_fn = function(n, kx) 10L,
  methods = "iv_oracle",
  verbose = FALSE
)

head(raw_iv)
```

`summarise_iv_results()` aggregates to one row per `(method, design, n, kx, q)`
cell and includes local overidentification diagnostics when `q > 1`.

```{r summary}
tab_iv <- summarise_iv_results(raw_iv)
print(tab_iv, digits = 3)
```

## Paper Replication Scripts

The installed replication layer provides single-machine and SLURM entrypoints:

```{r full-run, eval = FALSE}
# Full main-grid run. Writes ./results/sim_iv_raw.rds and sim_iv_table.csv.
source(system.file("paper-replication/iv/run.R", package = "RdistNN"))
```

```bash
# On a SLURM cluster, after installing RdistNN:
sbatch /path/to/paper-replication/iv/hpc/submit.sh

# After the array tasks complete:
Rscript /path/to/paper-replication/iv/hpc/merge.R
```

Set `SIM_OUTDIR` before running these scripts to write results outside the
current working directory. The full grid uses 36 array cells and 10,000
replications per cell; package tests exercise the same scripts through a small
smoke grid instead of running the production simulation.
